title: Add per-request cost distribution and span enrichment for long-tail alerts
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Instrument runtime to emit per-request token-cost tags; add histogram aggregation and new long-tail alert rules. Backwards-compatible; no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: we see recurring incidents where a small fraction of requests (long tail) drive a disproportionate fraction of token cost and latency. Existing dashboards show aggregated averages and p99 latency but lack per-request cost histograms and span-level enrichment that would let SRE and product teams triage high-cost requests quickly. This change adds: 1) runtime span enrichment with per-request cost fields (token_count, token_cost_cents, route_category, quantization_profile, kv_cache_hit) so a single trace contains cost context; 2) a metrics ingestion step that builds per-route cost distributions (adaptive histogram buckets) enabling percentiles over cost and cost-per-token; 3) new console dashboard panels and a focused "long-tail cost" alert set that triggers on sustained P99 cost increases and on the ratio of cost contribution from top 5% requests; 4) a lightweight dynamic-sampling mechanism to record full spans for a sampled subset of high-cost requests to prevent overload. Implementation notes: instrumentation is opt-in via observability config; default sampling is conservative (0.1% overall, 5% for requests above soft-cost-threshold). Backwards compatibility: legacy traces without cost tags are handled by the dashboard and ingestion pipeline (null-safe). Rollout plan: feature flag behind devops/telemetry rollout; staged rollout to prod metrics cluster, then enable dashboard and alerts in Canary namespace for two weeks before global enablement. Related: ENG-3281 (dashboard work), ENG-3340 (alerts tuning).

review_thread: Miguel Santos: Nice end-to-end. One concern: how do we bound memory growth when we dynamically sample full spans for high-cost requests?
Aisha Patel: Implemented a backpressure circuit and per-worker sample cap (see cost_histogram_processor.py, comments). Added tests to simulate burst and ensure we drop safely.
Claire Huang: Can we make the default soft-cost-threshold environment-configurable and document recommended values?
Aisha Patel: Yes — moved threshold to values-observability.yaml with explanatory comment and added section in console dashboard README.
Evan Brooks: CI caught flaky test on first run, reran and all green. Approving pending one small linter nit.
Evan Brooks: linter nit fixed in a follow-up commit; approving.
notes_for_release: Enable feature flag in canary and monitor new dashboard panels for two weeks. If top-5% cost ratio exceeds 60% for any route for two consecutive days, increase sampling to 1% in that route and open ENG-ops ticket. Default thresholds are conservative; customers on Dedicated can opt-out via observability.enable_cost_enrichment=false.
migration_steps: Deploy telemetry service with cost_histogram_processor to metrics cluster
Enable alerts/long_tail_cost_rules.yaml in canary, monitor for 48h before global rollout
post_merge_actions: Create follow-up to add Docs reference and example queries (ENG-3399)
Coordinate with SRE to add runbook for long-tail cost incidents
Monitor metrics-ingestion CPU for first 72 hours post-rollout
notes_on_privacy: Per-request cost values are derived from token counts and model pricing. No user prompt content is stored in the new fields; spans only reference token counts and model metadata. Telemetry respects existing PII scrubbing rules.
perf_result_summary: Synthetic load test: P99 cost aggregation added ~2.8% CPU on telemetry workers at peak ingestion; dynamic sampling kept span export load within acceptable SLOs. Histogram memory footprint tuned with 64-bit counters and rolling window eviction.
